body_markdown:
If you’re like us—and if you’ve found this, then you probably are—you could debate the finer points of automotive design and engineering for an eternity. What just about every car fanatic can agree upon, however, is that owning just one is never enough. All of us have particular roles we need our vehicles to fill. Some vehicles are great at several, but we ask such a wide variety of tasks from our machines that it’s just not feasible for one to do everything well. Each of us has a magic number of cars; ours are below. Let us know yours in the comments.


## A Few for Nate


Chevrolet


I’ve experienced as many as three cars under my care simultaneously, and in my current space/life situation, that feels like the top end of what would make sense.


I’ll keep my 2016 GMC Sierra 1500 as my daily driver/work tool, because the utility of a truck can’t be denied—and it’s the perfect machine to carry my small family and our doofus Golden Retriever.


Then I’d like a car that I can drive in a spirited manner at autocrosses and track days, but that won’t be miserable for winding roads. For that, I’ll take a C5 Corvette Z06. I finally had a chance to drive a C5 earlier this year, and holy smokes, what a lovely machine.


For number three, I’d like something that can venture off the beaten path and chase mountain roads. Give me an 80 Series Toyota Land Cruiser kitted out with a light lift, 33-inch chunky tires, a good roof rack, and ARB bumpers front and rear. Overlanding is my favorite way to enjoy nature and automobiles at the same time, so this is a natural fit for me. — *Nathan Petroelje*


## A Half-Dozen…and Maybe One More


[Eddy Eckart](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/eeckarthagerty-com/)


There were nine cars under one roof before I realized I might have a problem. The current fleet sits at six; that seems like a healthy number. I’m[no longer overwhelmed by projects](https://www.hagerty.com/media/our-garage/garage-reboot-how-i-reinvigorated-my-automotive-passion/) , nor is there any looming guilt for not putting them to use. My big five-oh is closing in on three years away, though, and I am already plotting the next (commemorative) addition… — *Eddy Eckart*


## Somewhere in the Single Digits


Ford


My fleet is comically double-digit excessive and must be pared down soon. I’d like to keep the Jeep J-10, the first-gen International Harvester Scout, and a ratty Datsun 240Z, and maybe the 2006 Mini Cooper. I’d like to add a nice Torch Red C5 Chevy Corvette with a manual transmission, and maybe a big people mover like a Ford Excursion with the rare 5.4-liter V-8 (most came with the V-10 or the diesel engine) or the honkin’, one-meticulous-owner Chevrolet Suburban I owned until the mobile mechanic tried too hard to crank it using an overdose of ether-based starting fluid, which caught on fire. I’ll never forget the sight of the Suburban, yanked away by a wrecker, headed for the junkyard. The mechanic asked me if I still wanted him to work on that car over there next: Uh, no, I don’t think so. — *Steven Cole Smith*


## 13, if You Count Bikes


[Kyle Smith](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/kyle-smith/)


Just cars? Probably five. Maybe seven. It gets hard to drive or enjoy everything once you exceed the number of days in the week, though I have never really been that close to that number.


It makes sense, though: one sporty car, one aging sporty car, one old car, a pickup, something that doesn’t make any sense, and a daily driver. Pepper in one or two projects and that’s both a full shop and full calendar to keep all of them ready to drive.


And for me, those five cars would only be the start because you need at least eight motorcycles to go with that fleet…—Kyle Smith


## Lucky 7


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


I’ve only ever worked my way up to four before, but mostly by accident because I’m quicker to buy things than I am to get rid of them. If I scan the more intentional and slightly more ambitious garage of my daydreams, I count… Seven cars.


There would be a small, modern convertible (probably a Miata) for get-in-and-go top-down driving. There would be a ’60s sports car of some kind (like an Elan or an E-Type) for more deliberate drives. There would be a French oddball of some kind (like a Citroën 2CV) for slow drives. There would be a land yacht (not married to any particular badge, but I lean GM) for comfy cruising. Since I’m daydreaming, the last three spots go to an old formula car of some sort for vintage racing, a modern or modern-ish track car, and a truck to tow with.— *Andrew Newton*


## 6 to Cover All Bases


Porsche


Yesterday I had four cars. Today I have three. None is particularly interesting, however, so for this exercise, if I wanted to devise the most interesting and ideal fleet, I would have six. Specifically: A British roadster for the very best days; a sporty German coupe for every other day; a fast Swedish wagon; a slow old American pickup truck for house projects and dump runs; a Japanese minivan for general life requirements; an FJ60 Land Cruiser for slow escapes. — *Stefan Lombard*


## 4: Half for Utility, Half for Fun


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


I love our Prius for commuting duty, so that occupies the first parking space, and checks boxes for “commuter” and “road tripper.” For maximum convenience, I’ll add a Ford Maverick as a second daily driver. The rationale: I want something to haul small loads of soil or mulch, and the occasional Facebook Marketplace furniture find, but I don’t need to tow anything, and I refuse to drive a Honda Ridgeline before I have gray hair. Then, for the fun stuff: Something open-air and off-road-friendly, for weekends at Michigan lakes. Let’s say … first-gen 4Runner. I can’t imagine the ideal automotive life without something suited for back roads, so I’ll expand my ideal garage to four with a vintage Alfa Romeo Giulia. To really maximize convenience, I’ll keep it at my parents’ house in Georgia, within shouting distance of mountains, which Michigan is rather short on. Thanks, Mom and Dad! Feel free to drive it whenever.— *Grace Jarvis*


## 3 for Gillogly


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


I went down from three vehicles to two last year when I sold my pickup, and I miss the utility of having a bed to throw stuff into. As much as I love the roominess and efficiency of the ZR2 Silverado 1500 diesel, a 4×4 mid-size pickup fits the bill nicely. A GMC Canyon AT4X would be the ultimate late-model option and serve as a daily driver and a basecamp for weekend off-road activities. I have a feeling I’d regret selling my Cherokee, so I’ll hold onto that for now unless a Jeep Commando project pops up. That leaves my Pontiac LeMans, which I’ve lost interest in and don’t really drive anymore. I’d prefer to swap that for another classic that is a bit sportier. Since an Iso Grifo A3/C is not in the cards, perhaps another Pontiac like a ’70-73 Firebird or an early C3 Corvette to handle the local canyon roads. If I had that as my small, personal fleet, pretty much all of my automotive needs would be met, although I’m sure there would always be a desire to add one more project. — *Brandan Gillogly*
